mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local notarization followed exclusively by either Hague Apostille from the designated competent authority if the origin state is an Apostille Convention Contracting State, or Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention Contracting State. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Local notarization followed exclusively by either Hague Apostille if the origin state is an Apostille Convention Contracting State, or Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention Contracting State. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank seal and authorized signatory verification followed exclusively by either Hague Apostille if the origin state is an Apostille Convention Contracting State, or Consular Legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate if the origin state is not an Apostille Convention Contracting State. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories and transaction counterparties must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, European Union consolidated sanctions lists, and applicable China domestic sanctions and export-control lists. Screening must be refreshed before signing and again at name approval; adverse media, PEP status, family members, close associates and previous regulatory enforcement must be documented. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth evidence and senior-management approval. Any sanctioned or negative match must be immediately escalated.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration and Name Pre-approval System, supplemented by the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) public retrieval database at gsxt.gov.cn for same-name and conflict searches.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE must have a simplified Chinese statutory name arranged in the mandatory four-tier order: administrative division, trade name, industry or business characteristic, and organizational form. The trade name must be at least two Chinese characters and may not consist solely of English letters or pinyin; foreign brand transliteration must be phonetically recognizable and supported by evidence. An English name may be auxiliary but cannot replace the Chinese statutory name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name application may be appealed within 60 days by submitting a written administrative reconsideration request to the next higher market regulation authority. The request must include the original application number, the rejection decision, the proposed name, and evidence of the name retrieval search. If the reconsideration authority upholds the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent People's Court within six months. The applicant may also apply for an extension before the name reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and commercial mailbox solutions are generally not permissible for a WFOE registered office. China requires a fixed physical premises with a valid lease, property ownership document, or written landlord consent. Municipal tax authorities and licensed banks routinely conduct on-site verification and reject mail-only addresses. For ISIC 7310 AdTech DSP/SSP activity, even where no statutory license is triggered, the absence of a physical office will defeat bank account opening and tax registration. Certain free trade zones permit address clustering for approved technology businesses, but this is a narrow exception and still requires a supervised physical service address; pure mailbox arrangements remain unacceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: lease agreement, property ownership certificate or landlord authorization, rental payment receipts, utility invoices, staff attendance logs, payroll and social insurance records, office equipment, corporate signage, original business license, corporate seal storage, financial records, tax invoices, and any server or hardware relevant to the AdTech operation. Quantified risk: newly registered WFOEs face an estimated 20-35% annual probability of a short-notice or unannounced 'double random, one open' inspection by municipal market regulation or tax authorities in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities during the first 12 months.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 2-5, 23-57 and 63-75; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019, effective January 1, 2020), Articles 6-8 and 13-14; Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746), Articles 3-16.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Enterprise Registration Department of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), exercised at municipal/district level by the local Administration for Market Regulation through the province-level E-Registration portal and the National Enterprise Registration Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application, also filed as the Notice of Establishment Registration for a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the Articles of Association, shareholder decision, officer appointment forms, and SAMR-mandated verification schedules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on this ordinary WFOE, and no blocked escrow bank account is required at incorporation. Under Article 47 of the PRC Company Law (2023 Revision), the registered capital stated in the Articles of Association must be agreed in writing and fully paid in by shareholders within five years from the date of establishment unless law, regulation, or the Articles require an earlier date. If the Company later enters a regulated sector such as value-added telecommunications, finance, or insurance, a separate sector-specific minimum registered capital and paid-in capital rule may apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CN WFOE LTD

WHEREAS, CN WFOE LTD (the Company) is a limited liability company proposed to be organized under the laws of the People's Republic of China as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise; and

WHEREAS, the initial shareholder has approved the Articles of Association and has nominated the undersigned director to act as the first board; and

WHEREAS, in order to satisfy the registration conditions of the State Administration for Market Regulation and to permit the Company to commence corporate operations, the board must lawfully approve the share capital subscription, adopt the registered office, authorize banking channels, and appoint statutory officers.

NOW, THEREFORE, the board resolves as follows:

1. Share Capital and Subscription. The registered capital of the Company shall be the amount stated in Article [●] of the Articles of Association. The subscription of the sole shareholder is accepted, recorded, and ratified. The board instructs management to collect capital contributions in accordance with the capital contribution schedule and to ensure that the registered capital is paid in full no later than five years from the date of issue of the business license or by such earlier date as required by law.

2. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be the address set out in the Articles of Association, which shall be a lawful commercial address within the jurisdiction of the relevant Administration for Market Regulation. Management is authorized to execute a lease, obtain the landlord's property ownership and lease-usage certificate, and file the address with the registration authority.

3. Banking Authorization. The chief financial officer or such other person as the legal representative may designate is authorized to open RMB and foreign currency bank accounts with licensed commercial banks, execute account documents, set up internet banking with dual control, accept shareholder remittances, and perform all acts to obtain clean evidence of paid-in capital.

4. Statutory Officers. [●] is appointed legal representative and executive director; [●] is appointed supervisor; [●] is appointed general manager. These appointments shall take effect upon issuance of the business license and continue until replaced by the shareholder.

5. Filing and Implementation. The legal representative and any authorized agent are empowered to complete all market entity registration filings, tax registrations, seal carving, statistical declarations, and regulatory filings. Any two authorized signatories may execute instruments, provided that company seal and finance seal controls are observed.

6. Ratification. All pre-incorporation acts performed by the promoters on behalf of the Company are ratified to the extent they are consistent with the Articles of Association. This resolution shall be delivered to the relevant authorities with the establishment registration application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Reservation and Foreign Investor Qualification Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR-authorized National Enterprise Name Registration System and the local Administration for Market Regulation name-reservation queue.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-reservation application for the proposed Chinese company name of the WFOE, together with a transliterated English name. The system will check the name against registered enterprise names and prohibited characters. The application must identify the legal person shareholder, proposed business scope, and registered address. Once reserved, the name is held for six months and may be extended once if required. After preliminary approval, verify the foreign parent's nationality and corporate capacity are not restricted under the Foreign Investment Negative List; if the negative list applies, adjust the business scope or ownership structure before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name reservation application form
Three candidate names with Chinese and English transliterations
Identity or qualification documents of the sole foreign shareholder
Power of attorney to the incorporation agent if filing through a representative
Proposed registered address confirmation and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected because of confusing similarity or prohibited elements, file a new name reservation application containing up to three alternative names. If rejection is based on the Foreign Investment Negative List, revise the business scope or ownership structure before re-filing. For administrative error, request an internal review from the local Administration for Market Regulation within seven working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Apostille and Chinese Translation of Foreign Investor Dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foreign notary authority of the investor's jurisdiction, PRC consular post or apostille authority designated under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention as implemented in China since November 7, 2023, and a certified Chinese translation agency.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the foreign parent's certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, board authorization, director passport copies, and bank reference letter to a local notary or other competent authority. If the parent is in a Hague Apostille jurisdiction, obtain an apostille; if not, follow PRC consular legalization. Deliver all original and duplicated documents to a certified translation agency to produce Chinese translations bearing a seal and translator's certification. Ensure the documents are current and contain no conflicting signatures; the translation must match the notarized original names. Corporate capacity verification must be finalized before AMR submission.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation of the foreign parent
Certificate of good standing issued within six months
Board resolution of the foreign parent authorizing the establishment of the WFOE
Passport copies of directors and shareholders
Bank reference letter for the foreign parent
Apostille certificate or PRC consular legalization for each public document
Certified Chinese translation of each document and apostille
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an apostille is deemed deficient, return the document to the issuing authority for replacement or use PRC consular legalization. If a Chinese translation is challenged, engage another certified translator, attach the translator's license and a revised translation, and preserve the original notarized source documents for the record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Company Establishment Registration to Administration for Market Regulation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) enterprise registration division or the province-level online E-Registration portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the establishment registration application using the approved name. All statutory documents must be executed by the sole shareholder or authorized representative, and signatures must be consistent with the foreign investor's apostilled documents. Upload scanned originals or present hard copies at the local AMR service hall. Include the Articles of Association, shareholder decision, supervisor and legal representative consent forms, and address proof. The AMR will examine the lawfulness of the business scope, capital contribution schedule, and governance structure. Upon approval, the AMR issues a business license with a unified social credit code. Online review time usually counts from the day the application package is complete.
required_dossiers: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment Registration Application
Articles of Association signed by the sole shareholder or authorized representative
Shareholder decision appointing the legal representative, executive director, supervisor, and general manager
Approved name reservation notice
Commercial lease contract with property ownership certificate or lease-usage certificate
Apostilled and translated foreign investor qualification documents
Identity documents of the legal representative, supervisor, and manager
Consent forms for the designated legal representative and supervisor
Mandatory online or offline verification forms required by the local AMR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a correction or suspension notice, respond in writing within the statutory correction period, normally ten working days, and resubmit corrected pages. If the AMR refuses registration, the applicant may request an administrative reconsideration within 60 days or file an administrative lawsuit within six months under the Administrative License Law and Administrative Reconsideration Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Seal Carving, Bank Account Establishment and Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving unit, and a licensed commercial bank with SAFE-delegated foreign exchange registration authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the business license is issued, take the legal representative to a PSB-authorized seal engraving unit to carve and file the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal. Use the seals to open a basic deposit account and a foreign currency capital account at a licensed bank that can complete SAFE foreign exchange registration. The bank will require know-your-customer documentation and beneficial ownership declarations. Submit the foreign direct investment registration and obtain a capital account confirmation. For any shareholder remittance, the bank verifies the payment purpose and compliance before crediting the amount as paid-in capital.
required_dossiers: Original business license
Legal representative original identity document
PSB seal registration certificate
Carving confirmation for company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Bank account opening forms and KYC declaration
Beneficial ownership structure declaration
Foreign-Invested Enterprise foreign exchange registration form
Registered office lease agreement and property certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE raises a compliance query, respond with enhanced beneficial ownership and source-of-funds documentation. If the bank refuses an account due to internal policy, obtain a written refusal and approach another bank with SAFE-delegated authority or contact the local SAFE branch for clarification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Social Security, Statistics and Post-Registration Regulatory Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, local Statistics Bureau, and the municipal one-stop comprehensive service window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register tax information with the local tax office through the online e-tax bureau, obtain or confirm the taxpayer identification number, determine VAT taxpayer status and invoice quota, and execute the tax-bank settlement agreement. If employees are engaged, complete social insurance and housing fund registration with the local authorities. Submit statistics and set up the annual report filing account. If the entity will receive foreign exchange revenue, complete the SAFE reporting through the bank. Keep a timestamped filing record for each registration. The five-day SLA begins only after the business license data has been synchronized into the government databases. Timely filings prevent late penalties and ensure the entity can issue invoices and process payroll.
required_dossiers: Business license
Legal representative identity document
Registered office lease or property ownership certificate
Articles of Association
Bank basic deposit account opening certificate
Tax registration application form
Initial payroll plan and identity documents of any staff members
Social insurance registration form if applicable
Statistics registration form
Foreign exchange filing record if capital remittance is planned
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security records do not match AMR data, request a data synchronization correction through the local AMR and the e-tax bureau. If late filing penalties are threatened, submit an explanation and voluntary correction promptly. Use the 12366 tax hotline and 12333 social security hotline for procedural cure guidance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - this is a pure digital/consulting AdTech entity with no physical factory, assembly plant, chemical operation, or warehousing facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehouse operating permit is required at Stage 2. Internet information service licensing, if any, is outside industrial licensing and will be assessed separately under the ISIC 7310 commercial scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Ministry of Ecology and Environment has no formal EIA jurisdiction over a non-construction, office-only digital service operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - no construction project, industrial installation, or land-changing activity is within the Classified Management List for Environmental Impact Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no process wastewater discharge, VOC emission source, or hazardous waste generation arises from the Company's operations; only ordinary municipal domestic water, sewage, and office waste disposal apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit or industrial occupational clearance is required for a pure office-based digital advertising platform. The Company must still occupy lawfully constructed commercial premises with valid fire acceptance and maintain ordinary office health and safety conditions as required by local building and labor regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online taxpayer portal: the 'Electronic Taxpayer' (e-Tax) environment accessible through the national tax service platform at www.chinatax.gov.cn and through each provincial-level electronic tax bureau portal under the STA's unified identity authentication system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor establishing a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) in Mainland China must first incorporate the entity with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). The business license issued by SAMR contains the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration identifier accepted by the STA. The WFOE must then complete tax registration in the provincial electronic tax bureau within 30 days of obtaining the business license; the data is synchronized from SAMR through the national 'one-time license and one-time tax registration' information-sharing mechanism. The WFOE must verify its tax types, filing period, corporate income tax regime, withholding obligations, and VAT taxpayer status in the e-Tax system using its legal representative's digital certificate or e-tax login. For a foreign non-resident enterprise with no permanent establishment in China that earns China-source income, the non-resident enterprise obtains a TIN by having the Chinese payer or withholding agent register the non-resident enterprise in the STA's non-resident tax management module and withholding registration system. The resident WFOE, once registered, uses the same USCC for all corporate income tax, VAT, customs, and cross-border tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election under its corporate income tax law. A WFOE is mandatorily treated as a Chinese tax resident enterprise and taxed at entity level on its worldwide income. The only relevant statutory election is the VAT administrative election: a WFOE with annual taxable sales below RMB 5,000,000 may elect to become a General VAT Taxpayer, and a Small-Scale Taxpayer may elect simplified levy treatment; these are indirect tax administrative elections, not entity classification or hybrid mismatch elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no turnover threshold for basic VAT/tax registration; every entity engaged in taxable supplies must register for tax. Mandatory General VAT Taxpayer registration applies once annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000 in local currency. Taxpayers with annual turnover below RMB 5,000,000 may remain Small-Scale Taxpayers, subject to simplified collection methods, unless they voluntarily elect General VAT Taxpayer status. For cross-border programmatic advertising services supplied within China to domestic customers, the output VAT rate is generally 6%; export zero-rating eligibility is governed by cross-border service rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates invoice issuance through the STA-controlled VAT invoice management framework, now operated under the Golden Tax System Phase IV. The fully digitalized electronic invoice regime requires taxpayers to issue electronic VAT invoices through the national electronic invoice platform; issuance data is transmitted to the STA in near-real time. Third-party invoice software providers must integrate with the STA through authorized APIs. Anti-fraud enforcement uses unique electronic invoice numbers, digital tax control codes, the taxpayer's digital certificate, and the electronic tax seal; there is no separate physical fiscal stamp, but the invoice data is subject to statutory audit and intelligent risk monitoring. Special VAT invoices for input credit must strictly comply with the STA's invoice data structural requirements and cannot be manually fabricated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods, zero-rated VAT applies to goods exported from the customs territory of China, provided the export is actually declared, shipped, and cleared by customs. For services, zero-rated VAT applies to qualifying cross-border taxable services supplied by a Chinese entity to an overseas recipient where the service is wholly consumed outside China. Programmatic real-time ad exchange and SSP services may qualify as zero-rated cross-border services under CaiShui (2016) No. 36 and related clarifying circulars if the DSP/SSP platform supplies advertising decisioning, ad exchange, and monetization infrastructure to foreign ad platforms, foreign advertisers, or foreign publishers, and if the advertising inventory and audience data are not directed at China-sourced impressions or Chinese domestic advertisers. The service contract must show the overseas recipient and foreign consumption; the commercial invoice, payment receipt, and evidence that the service is rendered and used outside China are required. If the platform serves Chinese domestic advertisers or delivers advertising to audiences located in China, the service is taxable at the standard services rate of 6%, and zero-rating is unavailable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) and electronic customs export data
Bill of Lading or airway bill evidencing physical despatch from a Chinese customs port
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange receipt evidencing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Signed contract of sale or cross-border service agreement identifying the overseas buyer or service recipient
Commercial invoice with full description of the exported goods or digital advertising services
Packing list and certificate of origin (for goods shipments)
Service delivery and acceptance certificates for cross-border programmatic advertising services
Overseas consumption and non-China usage evidence, including ad-server geolocation reports, IP address records, publisher platform logs, and audience jurisdictional reports
The zero-rated export declaration and input VAT allocation workbook filed in the STA electronic tax system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may audit zero-rating claims retrospectively and deny the zero rate where the statutory documentation package is incomplete, the foreign exchange is not repatriated within the prescribed 180-day period, or the services are found to be consumed inside China. In a clawback scenario, all VAT credits previously refunded or offset are recovered, statutory late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.05% per day from the date the tax was due, and administrative penalties range from 50% to 500% of the evaded tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law of the People's Republic of China. Fraudulent export refund conduct, including forged customs declarations or fabricated foreign exchange receipts, is subject to criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. The State Administration of Foreign Exchange may also impose penalties for failure to repatriate export proceeds in accordance with the Administration of Settlement, Sale, and Payment of Foreign Exchange Provisions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC); State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated foreign exchange regulator
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese Renminbi is not fully convertible. Current account items, including cross-border digital advertising service fees, are generally freely convertible for trade in services once the transaction is validated by the designated bank and the amount is within the approved service trade scope. Capital account items, including inbound FDI equity contributions, debt financing, and external guarantees, remain subject to registration, approval, and investment-purpose verification. A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must handle its capital injection through an FDI registration with SAFE and must not divert registered capital into treasury products or offset losses without bank supervision. Profit remittance is permitted once annual statutory audit is completed, taxes on dividends are withheld, and the bank verifies the audited financial statements and tax payment certificates. Exchange-rate fluctuations may affect capital conversion because settlement of foreign currency capital into RMB follows the onshore spot rate at the bank's designated price; there is no free offshore convertibility. To achieve a borderless AdTech treasury, the WFOE must combine onshore bank accounts with foreign currency accounts for collection from overseas programmatic buyers and clearing through SWIFT. The entire treasury structure must be supported by underlying contracts, invoices, and audit trails to avoid being characterised as speculative cross-border gambling or trade misinvoicing, which could lead to SAFE penalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current PRC foreign exchange administration framework, there is no mandatory export-proceeds conversion ratio and no forced surrender requirement to the State for service trade receipts. However, all cross-border current account receipts must be repatriated into China and collected through a designated domestic bank account in a timely manner; the bank must verify the authenticity of the transaction before accepting the deposit. For goods trade, export proceeds are required to be collected within 180 days from the date of export customs declaration unless an approved extension exists. For digital advertising service receipts under ISIC 7310, the WFOE should invoice within the agreed billing cycle and receive the foreign exchange proceeds through the bank under the service trade verification system, submitting the service contract, commercial invoice, evidence of DSP/SSP delivery, and tax payment certificates. The bank will not apply a fixed conversion ratio, but the WFOE may voluntarily convert into RMB or hold the proceeds in a foreign exchange settlement account; if retained in foreign currency, the account balance must be supported by eligible current account receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account for Foreign Currency Capital Injection and Basic Deposit RMB Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operating RMB Settlement Account plus Current-Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Comprehensive Treasury Account for FX Settlement and Cross-Border Payment Collection

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not a compliant primary banking channel for the WFOE in Mainland China. The PBOC and SAFE have not opened the local RMB clearing system (CNAPS/CIPS) to unlicensed fintech EMIs; therefore an offshore EMI cannot legally maintain the WFOE's capital verification account, obtain the FDI registration, or complete annual tax remittance filings. An EMI can be used only in a non-establishment support capacity, such as collecting advertising receivables from selected markets before funds are swept into the onshore bank, provided the EMI does not hold any IBAN or RMB account in China and the WFOE has segregated deposit accounts. If the EMI has a licensed domestic banking partner, that partner must still be the account-holder bank of record for all capital and tax-related transactions. The overall viability is Low as a primary rail and Medium as a secondary collection tool, but it must never replace the tier-1 domestic bank for statutory capital or dividend repatriation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and the legal representative are generally required to be available for an in-branch interview when opening the WFOE's first onshore bank accounts. Physical presence can be established by the legal representative visiting the branch in person with original passport, board resolutions, articles of association, business license, and company chop. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard market practice in Mainland China; however, certain banks will permit an authorized officer to appear in person with a notarized and Chinese-language legalized power of attorney and board resolution if the legal representative is abroad, and may require a live video call or face-to-face verification at the Chinese consulate or bank head office. All directors named in the SAFE/FDI application must execute the required anti-money laundering questionnaires; a failure to appear or produce original identity documents will cause the onboarding committee to reject the application. Given the WFOE's AdTech business, expect an additional business-model interview covering the technology platform, delivery traffic verification, data flows, and the ultimate source of funds for advertisers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in beneficial ownership and offshore parent entity chain, with potential nominee shareholders or complex layered holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified organisational chart from the ultimate beneficial owner through every intermediate holding vehicle; copies of each entity's certificate of incorporation, register of directors and shareholders; notarised identification of all individuals with 10% or more economic interest or voting control; a board resolution authorising the WFOE account opening; and a legal opinion or notarised statement confirming the absence of anonymous shell structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the inbound FDI capital contribution, particularly from overseas VCs or family offices with insufficient banking record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish the signed capital subscription and contribution agreement, bank statements from the investing entity for the preceding 12 months, evidence of the investor's corporate net worth via audited financial statements, the original SWIFT MT103 onward transmission confirmation, and a signed declaration that the funds are not derived from proceeds of crime, together with the SAFE FDI registration certificate and shareholders' capital contribution schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade compliance concentration in programmatic advertising, where false ad invoicing can be used to disguise value transfers, and where counterparty sanctions exposure may rise through unknown DSP/SSP supply chain partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a detailed flow-of-funds and platform architecture map showing buy-side and sell-side counterparties, inventory providers, data management platforms, and publisher settlement routes; executed master service or ad-insertion contracts with each major counterparty; invoices, billing records, and measurement logs; an external audit opinion on ad traffic validity; and an internal sanctions screening policy with evidence that counterparty names, IP addresses, and digital wallet identifiers have been screened against United Nations, OFAC, EU, and PRC sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between expected annual turnover of the AdTech platform and the business substance, staffing, or office metrics that the WFOE presents to the compliance committee
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the latest business license with ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 scope in English and Chinese, substitution of local labour office or social insurance payment records for required staff, functional office lease or co-working agreement, technology stack description, platform user and traffic log extracts, bank fee income projections, and a two-year audited financial projection supported by signed client letters showing how the DSP/SSP revenue will earn the proposed turnover.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE shall first complete the SAFE Foreign-Invested Enterprise (FDI) registration and foreign exchange investment reporting through a tier-1 domestic bank. The overseas investor must wire the equity subscription in the original currency using a SWIFT MT103 from the remitter's own banking account, not from a third-party source. The SWIFT remittance information must clearly identify the remitter, account number, relationship to the WFOE, and a purpose code matching the SAFE Balance of Payments classification, such as 601011 for inbound FDI capital contribution; the receiving bank will perform capital verification, record the sum in the FDI Capital Account, and then permit conversion into RMB for approved uses. All capital utilisation must be made from the settled RMB compliance account and can be used for wages, materials, office expenses, and genuine advertising infrastructure costs within the registered business scope, but cannot be used for secondary project investment or domestic equity acquisition without SAFE approval. The WFOE must file the capital settlement conversion report to SAFE within 30 days of each settlement transaction and obtain a capital account bank confirmation for the annual audit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for advertising inventory, SSP inventory purchases, data enrichment, or overseas publisher payments should be transmitted primarily by SWIFT MT103 with full-payment instructions from the WFOE's onshore settlement account. For high-value recurring invoices to foreign technology vendors, the WFOE may open a documentary collection or commercial letter of credit if the vendor's treasury requires the protection of trade documents, although digital AdTech services generally do not have bills of lading and are better served by clean wire transfer. Domestic publisher payouts in RMB can be executed through CNAPS or ACH-like batch clearing, while cross-border payouts to independent third-party app stores, measurement partners, and ad verification firms should be sent via the domestic bank's cross-border wire channel using the contract and invoice as supporting documents. The bank will require the exact funds purpose code for service trade, withholding tax certificate for royalties or software charges if any, and the VAT invoice when processing outward payments; the WFOE should keep a treasury dashboard linking each SWIFT confirmation to the source DSP/SSP transaction ID to avoid duplication.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB forward contracts (deliverable) with genuine current account exposure under the SAFE real-need principle
Currency swaps and common FX swaps between RMB and USD/EUR for matching the timing of capital settlement, dividend repatriation, and vendor disbursements
FX options on small notional amounts for adverse-movement coverage where a tier-1 bank approves the required trade-background documents
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for onshore WFOE hedging, and onshore banks will require separated underlying transactions rather than index-only speculation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Credit Information Report and Foreign Investment Information Report (joint enterprise annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, jointly administered with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for foreign investment information reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate inclusion in the Operating Anomaly List after 30 June; monetary fine up to RMB 10,000 (approximately USD 1,400) for delayed or refused filing; three consecutive years of non-filing triggers inclusion in the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, administrative revocation of the business license, credit blacklisting, and market-access restrictions on directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Information Filing and Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 30 days of establishment; change filing within 30 days after a beneficial ownership change; annual re-confirmation embedded in the enterprise annual report window ending 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, late filing, or false beneficial ownership information is subject to correction orders and penalties up to RMB 50,000 (approximately USD 7,000) for the entity and up to RMB 10,000 for responsible persons; continued non-compliance triggers Operating Anomaly List inclusion and credit sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Related-Party Transaction Disclosure (Annual CIT Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), competent local in-charge tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for the preceding calendar year, unless statutory extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment surcharge of 0.05% per calendar day on the outstanding corporate income tax; administrative penalty from 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax for false or non-filed returns; forced collection through bank account freeze and asset seizure; downgrade to negative taxpayer credit and risk-based invoice restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory audit of financial statements and issuance of PRC CPA audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent PRC-licensed accounting firm; audit report is delivered to the shareholders, retained in the company register file, and made available to SAMR and the tax authority in support of the annual report and CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements for a 31 December year-end must be audited in time for shareholder approval by 30 April and in all cases before the 31 May CIT filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to audit prevents lawful dividend distribution and approved capital reductions; unaudited financial statements are not accepted as reliable for the enterprise annual report transparency index; losses and deductions may be challenged by the tax authority; directors and executive officers may incur personal liability for losses caused by breach of PRC Company Law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual FDI Equity and Interests Registration (Foreign Exchange Direct Investment Stock of Rights and Interests Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), local branch, through the digital foreign exchange registration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June using the SAFE existing FDI equity and interests registration module for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missed filing places the WFOE on the SAFE abnormal list, blocking cross-border dividend remittance, capital repatriation, and new foreign exchange bank registrations; administrative fines up to RMB 30,000 (approximately USD 4,200) may be imposed; the entity must complete a late online filing with an explanation and supporting documents before restrictions are lifted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All WFOEs are unconditionally within the mandatory audit scope. Under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law, every limited liability company must prepare annual financial reports at the end of each fiscal year and have them audited by an independent PRC-licensed certified public accounting firm. There are no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount de-minimis thresholds for a WFOE; annual certification by a PRC CPA is also a de facto condition for the enterprise annual report, foreign investment information report, and corporate income tax final settlement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE/CAS), substantially converged with IFRS; qualifying small enterprises may use the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but a cross-border WFOE in the AdTech platform business should apply full CAS. Audit work is governed by China Standards on Auditing (CSAs) issued by the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must identify and file its beneficial owner(s) (natural persons who directly or indirectly control not less than 25% of shares or voting rights, or who exercise control in another manner) with SAMR and PBOC. Registration is renewed annually through the enterprise annual report process with a 30 June deadline; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days after the change. The annual confirmation verifies the continuity of the UBO record and flags discrepancies, but does not require a separate notarized submission if the online annual report is completed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Shareholders' Meetings and Board Resolutions
Statutory Accounting Books and Financial Ledgers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,500 per year for a professional registered office or registered address agency; physical leased premises in major commercial cities will be materially higher
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,800 - USD 6,000 for a low-risk WFOE with programmatic advertising platform activity; USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 for group-audited, intercompany, or SEC-reporting subsidiaries

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for High and New Technology Enterprises; 100% super deduction for qualified R&D expenses; tax holidays for software enterprises (2-year exemption followed by 3-year 50% reduction); preferential effective rates for Small and Low-Profit Enterprises; technology transfer income exemption; Free Trade Zone preferential regimes; accelerated depreciation for fixed assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax System
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filing due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (by 31 May for calendar-year entities); quarterly provisional returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue (营业收入) from all business activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE, as a Chinese resident enterprise, reports worldwide income. For programmatic advertising, allocate revenue between China and overseas based on where services are performed, risks assumed, and contracts executed. Include platform fees, DSP/SSP commissions, and media-buying margins; reconcile related-party transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of operations (营业成本) including direct and indirect costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only substantiated business expenses supported by original invoices and vouchers. Intercompany service fees and royalties paid to offshore affiliates must satisfy the arm's length standard and beneficial ownership test; otherwise, add back for tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit (利润总额) derived from accounting books.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Derive profit from PRC GAAP financial statements. Align with audited accounts. For cross-border advertising services, apportion China-source income according to the actual location of economic activities and the Chinese PE threshold. Foreign-source income is taxable but eligible for foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments (纳税调整增加额/减少额) to convert accounting profit to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transfer pricing adjustments, non-deductible provisions, excess entertainment and advertising expenses, and exchange gains/losses. Claim treaty benefits and foreign tax credits in the relevant supplementary schedules. Adjust intercompany charges that are not at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (应纳税所得额) after all adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income after all add-backs and deductions. Losses can be carried forward for up to 5 years (10 years for High-Tech Enterprises if qualified). Ensure loss utilization is supported by annual loss reports and tax filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate (适用税率) and preliminary tax (应纳所得税额).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% statutory rate unless an approved HNTE 15% rate is available. Deduct quarterly provisional payments already made. For non-resident shareholders, the taxable profit in this box forms the basis for future dividend withholding tax when profits are distributed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits (境外所得抵免) and ultimate tax payable (应补退税额).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit foreign taxes paid on double-taxed income, limited to the Chinese tax that would be payable on that income. The box computes the final annual settlement. Dividend withholding tax on outbound distributions is not effected here; it is withheld separately at the time of payment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a fine of RMB 2,000–10,000 (RMB 10,000–50,000 for serious cases) plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Understating tax is subject to a penalty of 50%–500% of the underpaid amount. Criminal prosecution for tax evasion applies where the evaded amount exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable, leading to imprisonment up to 7 years and additional fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid by a Chinese resident enterprise to a non-resident corporate shareholder; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong DTA and other applicable treaties if the beneficial owner is a qualifying company with substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction and provide a notarised copy; (ii) complete a Beneficial Ownership (BO) self-declaration and supporting evidence demonstrating real economic substance, business purpose, and no pass-through arrangement; (iii) deliver these documents to the WFOE before the dividend is paid so the withholding agent can apply the reduced rate at source. If excess tax was withheld, the non-resident may file a refund application within three years through the withholding agent to the competent Chinese tax authority, attaching all treaty-benefit documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalties are subject to a statutory 10% withholding tax. Under applicable DTAs, the rate may be reduced to 7% or 5% (depending on the treaty, e.g., interest under China-Hong Kong is 7%, royalties are 5% under certain conditions), always conditioned on the recipient being the beneficial owner and not maintaining a permanent establishment in China.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation is mandatory if annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions. Master File preparation is mandatory if annual aggregated related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China enforces an economic substance doctrine through the General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) under Article 47 of the Tax Collection Administration Law and the Beneficial Ownership test under SAT Public Notice [2018] No.9. A WFOE must demonstrate substantive business activities, actual employees, premises, decision-making authority, and risk assumption to support intercompany contracts and to claim treaty benefits; otherwise, treaty benefits are denied and profits are re-characterised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating programmatic advertising revenues, fabricating invoices, or reporting inflated intercompany charges to offshore DSP/SSP affiliates located in zero or low-tax jurisdictions to shift profits out of China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law, evaded taxes are recovered with late-payment surcharge and a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law imposes imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines where the evaded amount exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or directly participated in the fraudulent arrangement are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid taxes and fines. They may face exit restriction (blacklisting), asset seizure, and criminal imprisonment for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, maintain, and submit the Local File and Master File within the statutory deadlines, or using non-arm's length prices for related-party dealings with overseas affiliates, causing understatement of Chinese taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under SAT Public Notice [2016] No.42 and Article 44 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, the tax authority may reassess taxable income using the appropriate transfer-pricing method and impose additional interest at the one-year loan base rate plus 5 percentage points per annum on the underpaid tax. Administrative fines under Article 64 of the Tax Collection Administration Law range from RMB 2,000 to RMB 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the company's failure to implement proper transfer-pricing policies. They may be subject to civil claims by the company, administrative exit bans, and, in aggravated cases, criminal liability for aiding tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse / False Beneficial Ownership Claim
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, royalties, or interest through a Hong Kong or other treaty jurisdiction conduit company with no economic substance, to claim a reduced DTA withholding rate (e.g., 5% on dividends) instead of the statutory 10%, while the ultimate beneficiary is elsewhere.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under SAT Public Notice [2018] No.9 and Article 47 of the Tax Collection Administration Law. The tax authority collects the underpaid withholding tax plus daily late-payment interest (0.05% per day) and imposes a penalty of up to 5 times the shortfall. If fraud is established, criminal tax evasion charges apply under the Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or approved the conduit arrangement are jointly and severally liable for the short-paid withholding tax. They may face travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal prosecution for fraudulent tax practices, with imprisonment of 3 to 10 years depending on the amount defrauded.
